Rafael / Priyom —

I've gone through the MediTrust redlines and annotated a prioritized list. Attaching a PDF summary as well (Redwood_privacy_counsel_comments_20270805.pdf). Key points below (with recommended Redwood positions):

1) Cross-border transfers (Section 7): MediTrust wants explicit reference to transfer mechanisms. Recommend: accept Standard Contractual Clauses (EU SCCs) + Redwood's EU-US Addendum. Counter-propose: insert SCCs as the default mechanism and add option language for additional safeguards (encryption in transit, access controls).

2) Subprocessors (Section 8): MediTrust asks for narrow carveouts for certain analytics vendors. Recommend: commit to providing current subprocessor list at execution and 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; reject open-ended prior consent requirement but offer escalation path for high-risk subprocessors.

3) Audit / inspection rights (Section 10): MediTrust's redline seeks on-site audit and unlimited access. Recommend: limit to SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) reports plus a mutually agreed remote evidence-sharing process; on-site audits only upon material breach or with 90 days' notice and scope limits.

4) Data retention / deletion (Section 12): Acceptable to confirm deletion timelines (30/90 days depending on data type) but push back on language implying perpetual access to backups. Propose clear deletion confirmation deliverable.

5) Indemnity & liability caps: MediTrust asked to increase cap; maintain current cap tied to fees for the 12-month period with carveouts for willful misconduct.

I've also drafted short language snippets for each item (see attachment). If Sales wants to make goodwill concessions, recommend offering a one-time SOC 2 attestation delivery and an agreed addendum for transfers rather than changing the liability cap.

I'll be available for a quick sync with Tom (MediTrust counsel) if you'd like to walk through our proposed text.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the redline and for the patience while we reviewed. Summary of Redwood's proposed positions based on Marissa's counsel review:

- Transfers: We'll accept EU SCCs as the default transfer mechanism and include Redwood's EU-US Addendum as an operational safeguard.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor roster at signing and give 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; for high-risk new subprocessors we will engage in an accelerated review and offer an escalation path.
- Audits: We will deliver SOC 2 Type II reports and agree to a remote evidence-sharing process; on-site audits are limited to material incident scenarios with scope/time limits.
- Retention/Deletion: We propose a 30-day secure deletion for most customer data and a 90-day window for archived/backups. We'll provide a deletion confirmation certificate upon request.
- Liability: Maintain standard liability cap (fees for prior 12 months) with carveouts for willful misconduct.

Attached is a short concessions matrix (RDW_DPA_Concession_Matrix_20270806.xlsx) that maps each MediTrust ask to our recommended response. If that aligns, I'll prepare a DocuSign envelope routing: MediTrust legal -> MediTrust signatory -> Redwood legal -> Redwood exec (electronic signature). Proposed DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelopes/1234-rt-mt-2027

Could Tom or Sara confirm that routing and the board timeline (8/12) still work on your side? If yes, we'll provision the envelope and target e-sign by 8/9 to meet exec review cycles.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
